text.content: And it came to pass that he gave battle again unto Shule, [c]1617513101[/c] the king; and he took Shule, the king, and carried him away captive into Moron. [c]1617412101[/c]

people.name: Noah2

places.info: North of the great land of Desolation

text.heading: Ether 7:18
text.content: And it came to pass as he was about to put him to death, [c]1617604101[/c] the sons of Shule crept into the house of Noah by night and slew him, [i]3500[/i] [c]1617604701[/c] and broke down the door of the prison and brought out their father, and placed him upon his throne in his own kingdom. [c]1617411101[/c]

people.name: Noah2
people.title: Early Jaredite king, son of Corihor2

narration.description: {Noah|noah2}’s son, also named {Cohor|cohor1}, takes {Noah|noah2}’s kingdom, but does not continue the siege against {Shule|shule}.

text.heading: Ether 7:19
text.content: Wherefore, the son of Noah did build up his kingdom in his stead; [c]1617218101[/c] [c]1617704101[/c] [c]1617713101[/c] nevertheless they did not gain power any more over Shule the king, and the people who were under the reign of Shule the king did prosper exceedingly and wax great. [c]1617604801[/c] [c]1617704701[/c] [c]1616506601[/c]

people.name: Noah2
people.title: Early Jaredite king, son of Corihor2

notes.title: “Build up his kingdom in his stead”
notes.text: Presumably in his home territory of the “land of their first inheritance” (Ether 7:16).

narration.description: The two {Jaredite|jaredites} kingdoms of {Shule|shule} and {Cohor|cohor2} go to battle—Shule’s kingdom wins, and kills {Cohor|cohor2}.

text.heading: Ether 7:20–21
text.content: And the country was divided; and there were two kingdoms, [c]1617804101[/c] [c]1617806601[/c] the kingdom of Shule, and the kingdom of Cohor, the son of Noah. And Cohor, the son of Noah, [c]1617804701[/c] caused that his people should give battle unto Shule, in which Shule did beat them and did slay Cohor.

people.name: Jaredites
people.title: Descendants of Jared, his brother, and his friends

notes.title: “And the country was divided; and there were two kingdoms”
notes.text: Or And the country was divided, and there were two kingdoms:
Cohor, Shule’s grandnephew, is twice identified as the son of Noah to distinguish him from the Cohor who was Noah’s brother (Ether 7:15).

narration.description: {Cohor|cohor2}’s son, {Nimrod|nimrod2}, surrenders the kingdom to {Shule|shule}, and the nation is unified.

text.heading: Ether 7:22
text.content: And now Cohor had a son who was called Nimrod; and Nimrod gave up the kingdom of Cohor unto Shule, [c]1617904801[/c] [c]1618013101[/c] [c]1618007201[/c] [c]1616502601[/c] and he did gain favor in the eyes of Shule; [c]1618004701[/c] wherefore Shule did bestow great favors upon him, [c]1618016601[/c] and he did do in the kingdom of Shule according to his desires. [c]1617711101[/c] [c]1618004101[/c]

narration.description: During {Shule|shule}’s days, many prophets come and preach to the people, admonishing them to repent or be destroyed.

text.heading: Ether 7:23
text.content: And also in the reign of Shule there came prophets among the people, [c]1618104701[/c] [c]1618102601[/c] [c]1618104101[/c] [c]1618113101[/c] [c]1618101201[/c] who were sent from the Lord, prophesying that the wickedness and idolatry of the people was bringing a curse upon the land, [c]1618118101[/c] [c]1618102602[/c] and they should be destroyed if they did not repent.

people.name: Jaredites
people.title: Descendants of Jared, his brother, and his friends

notes.text: This is the first mention of prophets in the Jaredite narrative; they will reappear at Ether 9.28. Note that the land is cursed, rather than the people; see 1 Ne 17.35n;Alma 45.16n.

narration.description: Many people reject the prophets, but {Shule|shule} enacts laws to prevent persecution; people repent and begin to prosper.

text.heading: Ether 7:24–26
text.content: And it came to pass that the people did revile against the prophets, [c]1618204701[/c] [c]1618304701[/c] and did mock them. [c]1618204101[/c] And it came to pass that king Shule did execute judgment against all those who did revile against the prophets. [c]1618317101[/c] And he did execute a law throughout all the land, [c]1618302601[/c] which gave power unto the prophets that they should go whithersoever they would; [c]1618312101[/c] and by this cause the people were brought unto repentance. [c]1618318101[/c] [c]1618304101[/c] And because the people did repent of their iniquities and idolatries the Lord did spare them, and they began to prosper again in the land. [c]1618117102[/c] And it came to pass that Shule begat sons and daughters in his old age.

people.name: Jaredites
people.title: Descendants of Jared, his brother, and his friends

notes.text: The king of the Lamanites will issue a similar decree at Alma 23.1–3.

narration.description: {Shule|shule}’s reign continues in peace and righteousness.

text.heading: Ether 7:27
text.content: And there were no more wars in the days of Shule; [c]1618104801[/c] [c]1618504101[/c] [c]1618504701[/c] and he remembered the great things that the Lord had done for his fathers in bringing them across the great deep into the promised land; [c]1618507201[/c] wherefore he did execute judgment in righteousness all his days.

narration.description: {Shule|shule}’s son {Omer|omer} becomes king, and has a son, {Jared|jared2}, rebels and leaves for the [land of Heth|heth], where he establishes a kingdom, and overthrows his father.

text.heading: Ether 8:1–3
text.content: And it came to pass that he begat Omer, [c]1618607201[/c] and Omer reigned in his stead. [c]1618604701[/c] And Omer begat Jared; and Jared begat sons and daughters. [c]1618713101[/c] And Jared rebelled against his father, [c]1618604101[/c] [c]1618813101[/c] [c]1618704701[/c] [c]1618602601[/c] and came and dwelt in the land of Heth. [c]1618713102[/c] And it came to pass that he did flatter many people, [c]1618718101[/c] [c]1618604801[/c] [c]1618716601[/c] [c]1618704101[/c] because of his cunning words, until he had gained the half of the kingdom. [c]1618713103[/c] [c]1618611101[/c] And when he had gained the half of the kingdom he gave battle unto his father, and he did carry away his father into captivity, [c]1618804101[/c] and did make him serve in captivity; [c]1618816601[/c] [c]1618606601[/c]

notes.title: “Shule Begat Omer and Reigned in His Stead”
notes.text: Chronology: Omer’s reign would be about 980–950 B.C.

notes.title: “Omer”
notes.text: Omer is the son of Shule, Shule being the great-grandson of Jared (see Ether 1:30).

narration.description: While in his son {Jared|jared2}’s captivity, {Omer|omer} has more children, two named {Esrom|esrom} and {Coriantumr|coriantumr1}, who resent their brother {Jared|jared2}’s actions; they gather forces, overthrow {Jared|jared2}’s kingdom, spare {Jared|jared2}, and restore the kingdom to their father {Omer|omer}.

text.heading: Ether 8:4–6
text.content: And now, in the days of the reigns of Omer he was in captivity the half of his days. [c]1618917101[/c] And it came to pass that he begat sons and daughters among whom were Esrom and Coriantumr; [c]1618811101[/c] And they were exceedingly angry because of the doings of Jared their brother, [c]1618904701[/c] [c]1619013101[/c] insomuch that they did raise an army and gave battle unto Jared. [c]1619104701[/c] And it came to pass that they did give battle unto him by night. [c]1618904101[/c] And it came to pass that when they had slain the army of Jared they were about to slay him also; and he plead with them that they would not slay him, and he would give up the kingdom unto his father. And it came to pass that they did grant unto him his life. [c]1619011101[/c] [c]1619104101[/c]

notes.title: “They Did Grant Unto Him His Life”
notes.text: But the generosity of the younger brothers in sparing Jared's life turned out to be a mistake.
A night battle was sufficiently unusual to merit mention.

narration.description: {Jared|jared2} feels sorry for the loss of his kingdom and power, but {his daughter|jareds-daughter} begins to devise a plan to get {Jared|jared2}’s kingdom back.

text.heading: Ether 8:7–8
text.content: And now Jared became exceedingly sorrowful because of the loss of the kingdom, for he had set his heart upon the kingdom and upon the glory of the world. [c]1619204701[/c] Now the daughter of Jared being exceedingly expert, [c]1619318101[/c] [c]1619313101[/c] and seeing the sorrows of her father, [c]1619312101[/c] thought to devise a plan whereby she could redeem the kingdom unto her father. [c]1619316601[/c] [c]1619204101[/c]

notes.title: “Now the daughter of Jared being exceedingly expert, and seeing the sorrows”
notes.text: 𝒫 sorrow

notes.title: “Expert”
notes.text: WB: “experienced; skillful.” One is usually an expert in some particular field; here the daughter of Jared has a generalized cunning.

narration.description: {She|jareds-daughter} suggests that they plot to kill {Omer|omer} by enticing a man named {Akish|akish} to decapitate {Omer|omer} in exchange for her hand in marriage.

text.heading: Ether 8:9–10
text.content:
Now the daughter of Jared was exceedingly fair. And it came to pass that she did talk with her father, and said unto him:

“Whereby hath my father so much sorrow? Hath he not read the record which our fathers brought across the great deep? [c]1619104801[/c] [c]1619413101[/c] [c]1619306601[/c] Behold, is there not an account concerning them of old, that they by their secret plans did obtain kingdoms and great glory? [c]1619211101[/c] [c]1619304101[/c] [c]1618601201[/c] [c]1619304701[/c] [c]1619412101[/c] [c]1619413102[/c]

And now, therefore, let my father send for Akish, the son of Kimnor; and behold, I am fair, and I will dance before him, [c]1619512101[/c] and I will please him, that he will desire me to wife; wherefore if he shall desire of thee that ye shall give [c]1619516601[/c] unto him me to wife, then shall ye say:

’I will give her if ye will bring unto me
_the head of my father, the king.’” [c]1619408201[/c]

notes.title: “The Record Which Our Fathers Brought Across the Great Deep”
notes.text: [See the commentary on 3 Nephi 3:9]

notes.title: “Hath he not read the record which our fathers brought across the great deep”
notes.text: Nothing further is known about this record, but see Ether 1.2–4.

notes.title: “The record which our fathers brought”
notes.text: Nothing more is known of this record, though it was apparently a version of the primeval history from Gen (see Ether 1.2–4).

notes.title: “Secret plans”
notes.text: The phrase is generally associated with the Jaredites in the BoM; see Alma 37.29,32.

notes.title: “Obtain kingdoms and great glory”
notes.text: Precisely what Jared had set his heart upon in Ether 8:7.

The plot is reminiscent of the daughter of Herodias at Mt 14.6–12 and Mk 6.19–29, but in the NT there is no marriage request and John the Baptist is actually beheaded, while Omer escapes (Ether 9.1–3).

narration.description: {Jared|jared2} calls for {Akish|akish}, and {Jared’s daughter|jareds-daughter} for {him|akish}—he immediately asks for her as wife.

text.heading: Ether 8:11
text.content:
And now Omer was a friend to Akish; [c]1619616601[/c] wherefore, when Jared had sent for Akish, the daughter of Jared danced before him [c]1619616602[/c] that she pleased him, [i]1073[/i] [c]1619604101[/c] insomuch that he desired her to wife. [c]1619613101[/c] And it came to pass that he said unto Jared:

“Give her unto me to wife.”

notes.title: “Omer was a friend to Akish”
notes.text: The observation adds an element of betrayal to the coup that will be reported at Ether 9.1.

narration.description: {Jared|jared2} tells {Akish|akish} that he can have her in exchange for {Omer|omer}’s head.

text.heading: Ether 8:12
text.content:
And Jared said unto him:

“I will give her unto you, if ye will bring unto me
_the head of my father, the king.” [c]1619511101[/c] [c]1619604701[/c]

narration.description: {Akish|akish} gathers his family around, and asks if they will be faithful to him.

text.heading: Ether 8:13
text.content:
And it came to pass that Akish gathered in unto the house of Jared all his [c]1619816601[/c] kinsfolk, [c]1619804101[/c] and said unto them:

“Will ye swear unto me that ye will be faithful unto me
_in the thing which I shall desire of you?” [c]1619804701[/c]

people.name: Jaredites
people.title: Descendants of Jared, his brother, and his friends

narration.description: They all swear a pact of secrecy to stand by {Akish|akish}.

text.heading: Ether 8:14–15
text.content: And it came to pass that they all [c]1619916601[/c] sware unto him, by the God of heaven, [c]1619913101[/c] and also by the heavens, and also by the earth, and by their heads, [c]1619912101[/c] that whoso should vary from the assistance which Akish desired should lose his head; and whoso should divulge whatsoever thing Akish made known unto them, the same should lose his life. [c]1619904701[/c] [c]1619904101[/c] [c]1619912102[/c] And it came to pass that thus they did agree with Akish. And Akish did administer unto them the oaths which were given by them of old who also sought power, [c]1620013102[/c] which had been handed down even from Cain, who was a murderer from the beginning. [c]1619804801[/c] [c]1620004101[/c] [c]1619801101[/c] [c]1620013101[/c]

notes.text: “God of heaven” is a characteristically post-exilic phrase, used only here in the BoM.

notes.title: “Cain, who was a murderer from the beginning”
notes.text: See Gen 4;Hel 6.26–27; cf.Moses 5.29–31in the LDS Pearl of Great Price.

narration.description: Thus, the secret oaths of the {devil|satan} came among the people.

text.heading: Ether 8:16–17
text.content: And they were kept up by the power of the devil to administer these oaths unto the people, to keep them in darkness, to help such as sought power to gain power, and to murder, and to plunder, and to lie, and to commit all manner of wickedness and whoredoms. [c]1620113101[/c] [c]1619811101[/c] And it was the daughter of Jared who put it into his heart to search up these things of old; [c]1620213101[/c] and Jared put it into the heart of Akish; wherefore, Akish administered it unto his kindred and friends, [c]1620216601[/c] leading them away by fair promises to do whatsoever thing he desired.

notes.text: The phrase sought power to gain power highlights the insatiable nature of avarice and ambition.
“Kindreds and friends” are also associated with secret combinations at 3 Ne 6.27–28; 7.6.

narration.description: This is contrary to the will of the {Lord|god}, who does not work in secret combinations.

text.heading: Ether 8:18–19
text.content: And it came to pass that they formed a secret combination, [c]1620004701[/c] [c]1620404101[/c] [c]1620313101[/c] even as they of old; which combination is [c]1620316601[/c] most abominable and wicked above all, in the sight of God; [c]1620307201[/c] For the Lord worketh not in secret combinations, [c]1620104801[/c] [c]1620313102[/c] [c]1620404701[/c] [c]1620309101[/c] [c]1619403101[/c] neither doth he will that man should shed blood, [c]1620412101[/c] but in all things hath forbidden it, from the beginning of man. [c]1620301101[/c]

people.name: God
people.title: A reference to diety, be it Yahweh (יהוה); Jesus, or God the Father.

narration.description: The organized criminal ring of {Akish|akish} and his followers give him an advantage over {Omer|omer}.

text.heading: Ether 9:1–2
text.content: Therefore, behold, it came to pass that because of the secret combinations of Akish and his friends, [c]1621217103[/c] [c]1621204101[/c] [c]1621204701[/c] behold, they did overthrow the kingdom of Omer. [c]1621217102[/c] [c]1621202601[/c] [c]1621211101[/c] Nevertheless, the Lord was merciful unto Omer, and also to his sons and to his daughters [c]1621316601[/c] who did not seek his destruction.

people.name: Moroni2
people.title: Son of Mormon2, last of Nephites

notes.title: “and also to his sons and to his daughters who did not seek his destruction”
notes.text: 𝒫 to his sons and to his daughters which were not or which did not seek his destruction; 1837 to his sons and to his daughters who did not seek his destruction (JS)

narration.description: {Omer|omer} is warned in a dream to leave, and takes his family and those loyal to him to a place called [Ablom|ablom], on the coast.

text.heading: Ether 9:3
text.content: And the Lord warned Omer in a dream that he should depart out of the land; [c]1621418101[/c] [c]1621304701[/c] [c]1621304101[/c] [c]1621402601[/c] wherefore Omer departed out of the land with his family, [c]1621413101[/c] and traveled many days, and came over and passed by the hill of Shim, [c]1621413102[/c] and came over by the place where the Nephites were destroyed, [c]1621412101[/c] and from thence eastward, and came to a place which was called Ablom, [c]1621413104[/c] by the seashore, [c]1621413103[/c] and there he pitched his tent, [c]1621413105[/c] and also his sons and his daughters, and all his household, save it were Jared and his family. [c]1621311101[/c]

places.name: Ablom
places.info: Refuge for Omer and his family

notes.text: Lehi and Joseph (the husband of Mary), will similarly be warned in dreams to flee; see 1 Ne 2.1–2; Mt 2.13.

notes.title: “The place where the Nephites were destroyed”
notes.text: That is, the land of Cumorah; see Morm 6.

narration.description: In {Omer|omer}’s absence, {Jared|jared2} becomes king, and {Akish|akish} marries {Jared’s daughter|jareds-daughter}.

text.heading: Ether 9:4
text.content: And it came to pass that Jared was anointed king over the people, [c]1621417102[/c] [c]1621513101[/c] by the hand of wickedness; [c]1621504101[/c] [c]1621502601[/c] [c]1621504701[/c] [c]1621201201[/c] and he gave unto Akish his daughter to wife. [c]1621511101[/c]

notes.title: “By the Hand of Wickedness”
notes.text: Jared keeps his part of the bargain. He is anointed king, and he gives Akish his daughter, as promised.
Being anointed king by the hand of wickedness is a striking example of synecdoche, where a part stands in for the whole.

narration.description: {Akish|akish} plots against king {Jared|jared2}, and murders him; {Akish|akish} becomes the king in {Jared|jared2}’s stead.

text.heading: Ether 9:5–6
text.content: And it came to pass that Akish sought the life of his father–in–law; [c]1621604101[/c] [c]1621613101[/c] and he applied unto those whom he had sworn by the oath of the ancients, and they obtained the head of his father–in–law, as he sat upon his throne, giving audience to his people. For so great had been the spreading of this wicked and secret society that it had corrupted the hearts of all the people; [c]1621404801[/c] [c]1621604701[/c] therefore Jared was murdered upon his throne, [c]1621602601[/c] and Akish reigned in his stead. [c]1621611101[/c] [c]1621713101[/c]

notes.text: Once secret combinations are set in motion, they are difficult to control. In a turn of poetic justice, it was Jared, rather than Omer, who lost his head. Or in another BoM expression, his sins were literally “answered upon his own head” (Jacob 1.19; Mos 29.30–31).

notes.title: “Applied”
notes.text: WB: “to make request.”

narration.description: {Akish|akish} begins to be jealous of {his son|akishs-son}, so he locks him up in a dungeon, where he starves to death.

text.heading: Ether 9:7
text.content: And it came to pass that Akish began to be jealous of his son, [c]1621804101[/c] [c]1621812101[/c] therefore he shut him up in prison, and kept him upon little or no food until he had suffered death. [c]1621816601[/c] [c]1621804701[/c]

narration.description: {Nimrah|nimrah}, {Akish|akish}’s other son, becomes angry with his father, so he gathers a group of people who leave the kingdom, and join {Omer|omer} on the east coast.

text.heading: Ether 9:8–9
text.content: And now the brother of him that suffered death, (and his name was Nimrah) was angry with his father [c]1621916601[/c] because of that which his father had done unto his brother. [c]1621904101[/c] And it came to pass that Nimrah gathered together a small number of men, and fled out of the land, [c]1621804801[/c] [c]1621904701[/c] and came over and dwelt with Omer. [c]1621811101[/c] [c]1622013101[/c]

notes.title: “And now the brother of him that suffered death, (and his name was Nimrah”
notes.text: Nimrah is the brother, not the deceased prisoner.
Nimrah is the name of the brother, not the deceased prisoner.

narration.description: {Akish|akish} has {more sons|akishs-sons} who live and rule in wickedness; a power struggle develops between {Akish|akish} and {his sons|akishs-sons}.

text.heading: Ether 9:10–11
text.content: And it came to pass that Akish begat other sons, and they won the hearts of the people, notwithstanding they had sworn unto him to do all manner of iniquity according to that which he desired. Now the people of Akish were desirous for gain, [c]1622117102[/c] [c]1622104701[/c] even as Akish was desirous for power; [c]1622104801[/c] [c]1622213101[/c] wherefore, the sons of Akish did offer them money, [c]1622212101[/c] [c]1622104101[/c] by which means they drew away the more part of the people after them. [c]1622216601[/c] [c]1621201101[/c]

notes.text: Power can be bought as well as seized.

narration.description: A horrific civil war ensues, and the gross majority of {Akish|akish}’s kingdom is annihilated; the few survivors join {Omer|omer}’s kingdom, which now expands back into {Akish|akish}’s prior holdings.

text.heading: Ether 9:12–13
text.content: And there began to be a war between the sons of Akish and Akish, [c]1622304701[/c] [c]1622304101[/c] which lasted for the space of many years, yea, unto the destruction of nearly all the people of the kingdom, [c]1622404701[/c] [c]1621806601[/c] yea, even all, save it were thirty souls, [c]1622312101[/c] [c]1622313101[/c] and they who fled with the house of Omer. [c]1622318101[/c] [c]1622304801[/c] Wherefore, Omer was restored again to the land of his inheritance. [c]1622404101[/c]

people.name: Jaredites
people.title: Descendants of Jared, his brother, and his friends

notes.text: As prophesied at Ether 7.23.

narration.description: {Omer|omer}’s son {Emer|emer} is appointed to succeed {Omer|omer}, and after {Omer|omer}’s death, {Emer|emer} does in fact become king.

text.heading: Ether 9:14–15
text.content: And it came to pass that Omer began to be old; nevertheless, in his old age he begat Emer; and he anointed Emer to be king to reign in his stead. [c]1622504101[/c] [c]1622504701[/c] [c]1622111101[/c] [c]1622502601[/c] And after that he had anointed Emer to be king he saw peace in the land for the space of two years, and he died, having seen exceedingly many days, which were full of sorrow. [c]1622417101[/c] And it came to pass that Emer did reign in his stead, and did fill the steps of his father.

people.name: Jaredites
people.title: Descendants of Jared, his brother, and his friends

notes.text: Near annihilation under Omer (Ether 9:12) leads to more than two centuries of peace and righteousness under Emer, Coriantum, and Com.

notes.title: “Fill the steps of his father”
notes.text: Unique here, but see Ether 9:23.

narration.description: The {Jaredites|jaredites} prosper under {Emer|emer}’s reign, and have an abundance of strength, food, linen, minerals, and livestock.

text.heading: Ether 9:16–19
text.content: And the Lord began again to take the curse from off the land, [c]1622704101[/c] and the house of Emer did prosper exceedingly under the reign of Emer; [c]1622604801[/c] [c]1622704701[/c] [c]1622702601[/c] [c]1622804701[/c] and in the space of sixty and two years they had become exceedingly strong, [c]1622712101[/c] insomuch that they became exceedingly rich—having all manner of fruit, [c]1622913101[/c] and of grain, [c]1622813101[/c] and of silks, [c]1622813103[/c] and of fine linen, [c]1622813102[/c] and of gold, [c]1622813104[/c] and of silver, and of precious things; [c]1622704801[/c] [c]1622813105[/c] And also all manner of cattle, [c]1622913102[/c] of oxen, and cows, and of sheep, and of swine, [c]1622913103[/c] and of goats, and also many other kinds of animals which were useful for the food of man. [c]1623018102[/c] [c]1622916601[/c] [c]1622904701[/c] [c]1622804101[/c] [c]1622802601[/c] And they also had horses, [v]136[/v] [c]1623012101[/c] and asses, [c]1623013101[/c] and there were elephants and cureloms and cumoms; [c]1623018101[/c] [c]1623018103[/c] [c]1623012102[/c] [c]1623004101[/c] [c]1623013103[/c] all of which were useful unto man, [c]1623013102[/c] and more especially the elephants and cureloms and [c]1623016601[/c] cumoms. [c]1622611101[/c] [c]1623013104[/c] [c]1622901101[/c] [c]1623001201[/c] [c]1623004701[/c]

people.name: Jaredites
people.title: Descendants of Jared, his brother, and his friends

notes.title: “The curse”
notes.text: See Ether 7.23.

The animals listed in these verses are anachronistic from a New World perspective. It is noteworthy, however, that since the Jaredites preceded the law of Moses, there was no prohibition for them against swine. The identification of cureloms and cumoms is uncertain since the terms are unique to the BoM.

notes.title: “and there were elephants and cureloms and cumoms”
notes.text: These animals have not been identified.

narration.description: The {Lord|god} blesses the people, but the inhabitants of the land are to live unto the {Lord|god}, or face his wrath.

text.heading: Ether 9:20
text.content:
And thus the Lord did pour out his blessings upon this land, which was choice above all other lands; [c]1623104701[/c] and he commanded that whoso should possess the land should possess it unto the Lord, [c]1623104101[/c] or they should be destroyed when they were ripened in iniquity; for upon such, saith the Lord: [c]1623116601[/c]

“I will pour out the fulness of my wrath.”

people.name: God
people.title: A reference to diety, be it Yahweh (יהוה); Jesus, or God the Father.

places.name: The Promised Land
places.info: Land inhabited by the Jaredites, Lehites, and Mulekites

narration.description: {Emer|emer} lives righteously, sees {Jesus|jesus-christ}, and has many sons, one of whom is {Coriantum|coriantum1}, who succeeds {Emer|emer} as king.

text.heading: Ether 9:21–22
text.content: And Emer did execute judgment in righteousness all his days, [c]1622706601[/c] and he begat many sons and daughters; and he begat Coriantum, and he anointed Coriantum to reign in his stead. And after he had anointed Coriantum to reign in his stead he lived four years, and he saw peace in the land; [c]1623218101[/c] [c]1623204801[/c] yea, and he even saw the Son of Righteousness, [c]1623312101[/c] [c]1623302601[/c] [c]1623204101[/c] and did rejoice and glory in his day; [c]1623316601[/c] [c]1623111101[/c] [c]1623307201[/c] and he died in peace.

notes.title: “and he even saw the Son of Righteousness”
notes.text: ATV Sun of righteousness; cf. Mal 4.2; 2 Ne 26.9; 3 Ne 25.2

notes.title: “Son of Righteousness”
notes.text: Apparently referring to Jesus; see 2 Ne 26.8–9n;3 Ne 25.2n.

notes.title: “Rejoiced…in his day”
notes.text: Hel 8.22 (also referring to visions of the future Christ).

sections.title: The Reigns of Coriantum, Com, and Heth

narration.description: {Coriantum|coriantum1} also reigns righteously, but grows old without any children.

text.heading: Ether 9:23
text.content: And it came to pass that Coriantum did walk in the steps of his father, [c]1623402601[/c] [c]1623404101[/c] [c]1623406601[/c] and did build many mighty cities, [c]1623404701[/c] [c]1623413101[/c] and did administer that which was good unto his people in all his days. And it came to pass that he had no children even until he was exceedingly old.

narration.description: {Coriantum|coriantum1}’s wife dies, {Coriantum|coriantum1} remarries, has many children, and lives to be 142 years old.

text.heading: Ether 9:24
text.content: And it came to pass that his wife died, being an hundred and two years old. [c]1623513101[/c] And it came to pass that Coriantum took to wife, in his old age, a young maid, and begat sons and daughters; wherefore he lived until he was an hundred and forty and two years old.

notes.text: Like many of the figures in the primeval history of Gen, the Jaredites enjoyed improbable lifespans; cf. 2 Chr 24.15.

narration.description: One of {Coriantum|coriantum1}’s sons, {Com|com1}, becomes king; {Com|com1} has, among other children, a son named {Heth|heth1}.

text.heading: Ether 9:25
text.content: And it came to pass that he begat Com, and Com reigned in his stead; [c]1623602601[/c] and he reigned forty and nine years, [c]1623604701[/c] [c]1623604101[/c] and he begat Heth; and he also begat other sons and daughters. [c]1623411101[/c]

notes.title: “Com Reigned in His Stead”
notes.text: One of his sons, Com, probably the youngest, succeeded him.

narration.description: {Heth|heth1} begins to embrace the secret evil pacts of the past, hungers for power, and kills his father {Com|com1}, taking his place as king.

text.heading: Ether 9:26–27
text.content: And the people had spread again over all the face of the land, [c]1623713101[/c] [c]1623704101[/c] and there began again to be an exceedingly great wickedness upon the face of the land, [c]1623716601[/c] [c]1622613101[/c] [c]1623704701[/c] and Heth began to embrace the secret plans again of old, [c]1623804701[/c] [c]1623804101[/c] [c]1623702601[/c] to destroy his father. [c]1623712101[/c] And it came to pass that he did dethrone his father, for he slew him with his own sword; [c]1623718101[/c] [c]1623813101[/c] and he did reign in his stead. [c]1623711101[/c]

people.name: Jaredites
people.title: Descendants of Jared, his brother, and his friends

notes.title: “The people had spread again over all the face of the land”
notes.text: After the population was catastrophically reduced at the time of Omer, see Ether 9.12.

narration.description: Prophets come among the people and warn them to repent, warning them of a famine, but most people reject and harass the prophets.

text.heading: Ether 9:28–29
text.content: And there came prophets in the land again, [c]1623904101[/c] crying repentance unto them—that they must prepare the way of the Lord or there should come a curse upon the face of the land; [c]1623704801[/c] [c]1623904701[/c] [c]1623906601[/c] yea, even there should be a great famine, in which they should be destroyed if they did not repent. But the people believed not the words of the prophets, but they cast them out; [c]1624018101[/c] and some of them they cast into pits and left them to perish. [c]1624013101[/c] And it came to pass that they did all these things according to the commandment of the king, [c]1623911101[/c] Heth.

notes.title: “And there came prophets in the land again”
notes.text: Jaredite prophets were previously mentioned at Ether 7.23–25.
Jaredite prophets were previously mentioned at Ether 7.23–25.

notes.title: “Prepare the way of the Lord”
notes.text: The phrase echoes Isa 40.3, and its several allusions in both the NT and the BoM. In the Jaredite context, it is not clear when these prophets thought the Lord might come.

narration.description: The land is stricken with a dearth, the population declines rapidly, and venomous snakes attack people and scatter livestock.

text.heading: Ether 9:30–32
text.content: And it came to pass that there began to be a great dearth upon the land, [c]1624104701[/c] [c]1624104101[/c] [c]1624113101[/c] and the inhabitants began to be destroyed exceedingly fast because of the dearth, for there was no rain upon the face of the earth. [c]1624217101[/c] [c]1624113102[/c] And there came forth poisonous serpents also upon the face of the land, [c]1624104801[/c] [c]1624213101[/c] [c]1624112101[/c] [c]1624204101[/c] and did poison many people. [c]1624218101[/c] And it came to pass that their flocks began to flee before the poisonous serpents, [c]1624204701[/c] [c]1624212101[/c] [c]1624213102[/c] towards the land southward, which was called by the Nephites Zarahemla. And it came to pass that there were many of them which did perish by the way; nevertheless, there were some which fled into the land southward. [c]1624111101[/c]

people.name: Jaredites
people.title: Descendants of Jared, his brother, and his friends

notes.title: “There Were Some Which Fled into the Land Southward”
notes.text: The curse of drought and the pestilence by poisonous serpents devastated the Jaredites.

notes.title: “Dearth”
notes.text: WB: “scarcity; famine; barrenness.”
There was some overlap between Jaredite and Nephite territories, particularly in the latter part of each civilization, when the Jaredites fled south and the Nephites fled north.

narration.description: The {Lord|god} causes the snakes to form a barricade to block the people off from the southern land.

text.heading: Ether 9:33
text.content: And it came to pass that the Lord did cause the serpents that they should pursue them no more, but that they should hedge up the way that [c]1624416601[/c] the people could not pass, [c]1624413101[/c] that whoso should attempt to pass might fall by the poisonous serpents. [c]1624416602[/c]

people.name: God
people.title: A reference to diety, be it Yahweh (יהוה); Jesus, or God the Father.

notes.text: As with the rain, God also controls the snakes, which displace the Jaredites’ domesticated animals southward and prevent the people from following their flocks into territories that would later belong to the Nephites.

narration.description: The people try to follow the path of the migrating livestock, scavenging carcasses along the way.

text.heading: Ether 9:34
text.content:
And it came to pass that the people did follow the course of the beasts, and did devour the carcasses of them which fell by the way, [c]1624516601[/c] until they had devoured them all. [c]1624504101[/c]

[c]1624504701[/c]

people.name: Jaredites
people.title: Descendants of Jared, his brother, and his friends

notes.text: The repentance of the Jaredites in the face of famine prefigures the experience of the Nephites at the time of Nephi<sub >2</sub>; see Hel 11.7–17. Nevertheless, the poisonous snakes will remain a problem for several generations; see Ether 10.19.

narration.description: Seeing that their sins brought this upon them the people begin to repent; soon after, rain begins to fall, and fruit grows back in the northern region.

text.heading: Ether 9:34–35
text.content: Now when the people saw that they must perish they began to repent of their iniquities and cry unto the Lord. [c]1624411101[/c] And it came to pass that when they had humbled themselves sufficiently before the Lord [c]1624616601[/c] he did send rain upon the face of the earth; [c]1624304801[/c] [c]1624604701[/c] and the people began to revive again, [c]1624604101[/c] and there began to be fruit in the north countries, and in all the countries round about. [c]1624616602[/c] And the Lord did show forth his power unto them in preserving them from famine. [c]1624611101[/c] [c]1624607201[/c]

people.name: Jaredites
people.title: Descendants of Jared, his brother, and his friends

notes.title: “The Lord Did Show Forth His Power Unto Them in Preserving Them from Famine”
notes.text: Then rains came and the famine subsided.

narration.description: {Heth|heth1} dies in the famine, and his descendant, {Shez|shez1}, takes upon himself the task of reconstructing the ravaged nation.

text.heading: Ether 10:1
text.content: And it came to pass that Shez, [c]1624702601[/c] who was a descendant of Heth— for Heth had perished by the famine, [c]1624704101[/c] and all his household save it were Shez—wherefore, Shez began to build up again a broken people. [c]1624718101[/c] [c]1624704701[/c] [c]1624713101[/c]

notes.title: “And it came to pass that Shez, who was a descendant of Heth”
notes.text: Shez<sup>1</sup> was probably a son of Heth<sup>1</sup>; see Ether 1.25.

notes.title: “A descendant of Heth”
notes.text: Shez was probably a son of Heth; see Ether 1.25. It is remarkable that a king’s household—generally the most powerful, resource-rich members of society—would die in a famine.

notes.title: “Build up again a broken people”
notes.text: A poignant description of the task that faced the new king.

narration.description: {Shez|shez1} remembers the fate of his fathers, builds the kingdom righeously, remembering the good graces of {God|god}.

text.heading: Ether 10:2
text.content: And it came to pass that Shez did remember the destruction of his fathers, and he did build up a righteous kingdom; [c]1624804101[/c] for he remembered what the Lord had done in bringing Jared and his brother across the deep; [c]1624812101[/c] and he did walk in the ways of the Lord; and he begat sons and daughters. [c]1624711101[/c]

people.name: God
people.title: A reference to diety, be it Yahweh (יהוה); Jesus, or God the Father.

notes.title: “Remember the destruction of his fathers”
notes.text: A striking contrast with the regular BoM formula of remembering the captivity and deliverance of their fathers.

narration.description: {Shez|shez1} has a son (also named {Shez|shez2}) who begins to rebel against his father, but is soon enough attacked by a robber; his father it put back at ease.

text.heading: Ether 10:3
text.content: And his eldest son, whose name was Shez, [c]1624904101[/c] did rebel against him; nevertheless, Shez was smitten by the hand of a robber, because of his exceeding riches, which brought peace again unto his father. [c]1624704801[/c] [c]1624904701[/c]

notes.text: It is a sad commentary when the murder of a son is said to have brought peace to his father.

narration.description: {Shez|shez1} continues to reign righteously until his death; his other son named {Riplakish|riplakish} takes his place as king.

text.heading: Ether 10:4
text.content: And it came to pass that his father did build up many cities upon the face of the land, and the people began again to spread over all the face of the land. [c]1625004701[/c] [c]1625004101[/c] And Shez did live to an exceedingly old age; and he begat Riplakish. [c]1625013101[/c] And he died, and Riplakish reigned in his stead. [c]1624706601[/c]

narration.description: {Riplakish|riplakish} abuses his kingly power, imposes absurd taxes, lives in opulence, and has many wives and mistresses.

text.heading: Ether 10:5
text.content: And it came to pass that Riplakish did not do that which was right in the sight of the Lord, [c]1625112101[/c] [c]1625101201[/c] [c]1625104101[/c] for he did have many wives and concubines, [c]1625112102[/c] [c]1625113101[/c] and did lay that upon men’s shoulders which was grievous to be borne; [c]1625116601[/c] [c]1625113102[/c] yea, he did tax them with heavy taxes; [c]1625118101[/c] [c]1625004801[/c] and with the taxes he did build many spacious buildings. [c]1625116602[/c] [c]1624911101[/c] [c]1624701101[/c] [c]1625104701[/c]

notes.text: Concubines, heavy taxes, and extravagant buildings fit the BoM model of wicked kings, as with King Noah at Mos 11.1–2, 8–10.

notes.title: “Do that which was right in the sight of the Lord”
notes.text: V. 16 below, and fifteen times in 2 Kings and 2 Chron.

narration.description: {Riplakish|riplakish} builds a beautiful throne; he forces all his subjects to work, and pay taxes, and those unable to pay are thrown in prison, where they become his slaves.

text.heading: Ether 10:6
text.content: And he did erect him an exceedingly beautiful throne; and he did build many prisons, [c]1625216602[/c] [c]1625204701[/c] [c]1625204101[/c] and whoso would not be subject unto taxes he did cast into prison; and whoso was not able to pay taxes he did cast into prison; and he did cause that they should labor continually for their support; [c]1625117101[/c] and whoso refused to labor he did cause to be put to death. [c]1625216601[/c]

notes.text: Apparently skilled craftsmen were among those who either refused or were unable to pay taxes.

narration.description: {Riplakish|riplakish} exploits the imprisoned slaves and has them make all kinds of gold and ornaments.

text.heading: Ether 10:7
text.content: wherefore he did obtain all his [c]1625316601[/c] fine work, yea, even his fine gold he did cause to be refined in prison, [c]1625217101[/c] [c]1625313101[/c] and all manner of fine workmanship he did cause to be wrought in prison. And it came to pass that he did afflict the people with his whoredoms and abominations. [c]1625211101[/c]

narration.description: The people finally revolt, kill {Riplakish|riplakish}, and exhile his descendants.

text.heading: Ether 10:8
text.content: And when he had reigned for the space of forty and two years the people did rise up in rebellion against him; [c]1625416601[/c] [c]1625404701[/c] [c]1625404101[/c] and there began to be war again in the land, insomuch that Riplakish was killed, and his descendants were driven out of the land. [c]1625304801[/c] [c]1625413101[/c]

notes.text: This is the only reported populist revolt in Jaredite history.

narration.description: {Morianton|morianton1} was a descendant of {Riplakish|riplakish} who gathers some forces and conquers some cities back from the main body of {Jaredites|jaredites}; after more struggles and battles, he is successful in regaining the entire kingdom.

text.heading: Ether 10:9
text.content: And it came to pass after the space of many years, [c]1625417101[/c] Morianton, [c]1625502601[/c] [c]1625504101[/c] (he being a descendant of Riplakish) gathered together an army of outcasts, [c]1625516601[/c] and went forth and gave battle unto the people; and he gained power over many cities; and the war became exceedingly sore, and did last for the space of many years; and he did gain power over all the land, and did establish himself king over all the land. [c]1625411101[/c] [c]1625504701[/c] [c]1625501101[/c]

people.name: Jaredites
people.title: Descendants of Jared, his brother, and his friends

notes.title: “Outcasts”
notes.text: Members of the royal line who had been driven out in the previous verse.

narration.description: {Morianton|morianton1} is good to his people, and eases their burden, personally, however, is was not a moral or righteous man.

text.heading: Ether 10:10–11
text.content: And after that he had established himself king he did ease the burden of the people, [c]1625616601[/c] [c]1625712101[/c] by which he did gain favor in the eyes of the people, [c]1625504801[/c] and they did anoint him to be their king. And he did do justice unto the people, but not unto himself because of his many whoredoms; [c]1625618101[/c] [c]1625506601[/c] wherefore he was cut off from the presence of the Lord. [c]1625611101[/c] [c]1625604701[/c] [c]1625604101[/c]

notes.text: Morianton seems to have gained popular support by lowering taxes. Note that the phrase the people appears five times in Ether 10:9–12, as Morianton co-opts the people’s uprising in Ether 10:8 and restores monarchical rule.
The idea that a person might not “do justice” to himself because of sin is intriguing.

narration.description: {Morianton|morianton1}’s public policies lead to economic prosperity.

text.heading: Ether 10:12
text.content: And it came to pass that Morianton built up many cities, [c]1625804701[/c] [c]1625813101[/c] and the people became exceedingly rich under his reign, [c]1625804101[/c] both in buildings, and in gold and silver, and in raising grain, and in flocks, and herds, and such things which had been restored unto them. [c]1625816601[/c] [c]1625501201[/c]

sections.title: The Reigns of Kim, Kim’s Brother, Levi, Corom, and Kish

narration.description: {Morianton|morianton1}’s son {Kim|kim} eventually takes {Morianton|morianton1}’s place as king, reigns wickedly, and is overthrown by his brother; while in captivity, {Kim|kim} has a son named {Levi|levi2}.

text.heading: Ether 10:13–14
text.content: And Morianton did live to an exceedingly great age, and then he begat Kim; [c]1625913101[/c] [c]1625902601[/c] and Kim did reign in the stead of his father; and he did reign eight years, and his father died. And it came to pass that Kim did not reign in righteousness, wherefore he was not favored of the Lord. [c]1625811101[/c] [c]1625904101[/c] [c]1625904701[/c] And his brother did rise up in rebellion against him, [c]1626016601[/c] [c]1626004701[/c] [c]1626013101[/c] [c]1626004101[/c] by which he did bring him into captivity; and he did remain in captivity all his days; [c]1626012101[/c] [c]1626013102[/c] and he begat sons and daughters in captivity, and in his old age he begat Levi; and he died.

notes.text: The rebellious brother who took over the throne is never named.

narration.description: {Kim|kim} dies; {Levi|levi2} rebels against his uncle, and is successful in regaining the kingdom.

text.heading: Ether 10:15
text.content: And it came to pass that Levi did serve in captivity after the death of his father, [c]1626102601[/c] for the space of forty and two years. And he did make war against the king of the land, by which he did obtain unto himself the kingdom.

narration.description: {Levi|levi2} reigns righteously and prosperously, and his son {Corom|corom} succeeds him as king.

text.heading: Ether 10:16
text.content: And after he had obtained unto himself the kingdom he did that which was right in the sight of the Lord; [c]1626204101[/c] and the people did prosper in the land; [c]1626204701[/c] and he did live to a good old age, and begat sons and daughters; [c]1626004801[/c] and he also begat Corom, whom he anointed king in his stead. [c]1626011101[/c]

narration.description: {Corom|corom} also reigns righteously, and appoints his son {Kish|kish} to be the next king.

text.heading: Ether 10:17
text.content: And it came to pass that Corom did that which was good in the sight of the Lord all his days; [c]1626304701[/c] [c]1626304101[/c] [c]1626302601[/c] and he begat many sons and daughters; [c]1626313102[/c] and after he had seen many days he did pass away, even like unto the rest of the earth; and Kish reigned in his stead. [c]1626313101[/c]

narration.description: {Kish|kish}’s son {Lib|lib1} becomes king.

text.heading: Ether 10:18
text.content: And it came to pass that Kish passed away also, and Lib reigned in his stead. [c]1626404101[/c] [c]1626402601[/c] [c]1626413101[/c]

notes.title: “Kish Passed Away Also and Lib Reigned in His Stead”
notes.text: Chronology: The average-reign chronology places Kish at between 650 and 620 B.C.

narration.description: {Lib|lib1} is a righteous king; during his reign the barricade of snakes is destroyed, and the {Jaredites|jaredites} are able to travel south to become hunters.

text.heading: Ether 10:19
text.content: And it came to pass that Lib also did that which was good in the sight of the Lord. [c]1626502601[/c] And in the days of Lib the poisonous serpents were destroyed. [c]1626504101[/c] [c]1626504701[/c] [c]1626513101[/c] Wherefore they did go into the land southward, to hunt food for the people of the land, [c]1626513102[/c] for the land was covered with animals of the forest. [c]1626518101[/c] And Lib also himself became a great hunter. [c]1626304801[/c] [c]1626311101[/c]

people.name: Jaredites
people.title: Descendants of Jared, his brother, and his friends

notes.title: “The poisonous serpents”
notes.text: See Ether 9.31–33.

narration.description: The {Jaredites|jaredites} build a large city near the narrow neck of land; they become very prosperous and develop commerce, metalwork, and industry.

text.heading: Ether 10:20–23
text.content: And they built a great city by the narrow neck of land, [c]1626612101[/c] [c]1626613101[/c] by the place where the sea divides the land. [c]1626613102[/c] And they did preserve the land southward for a wilderness, to get game. [c]1626716601[/c] [c]1626713101[/c] [c]1626604101[/c] And the whole face of the land northward was covered with inhabitants. [c]1626604801[/c] [c]1626611101[/c] [c]1626713102[/c] And they were exceedingly industrious, [c]1626813101[/c] and they did buy and sell and traffic one with another, [c]1626804701[/c] that they might get gain. [c]1626804101[/c] And they did work in all manner of ore, and they did make gold, and silver, and iron, [c]1626913102[/c] and brass, [c]1626913103[/c] and all manner of metals; [c]1626904701[/c] [c]1626904101[/c] [c]1626913101[/c] and they did dig it out of the earth; wherefore they did cast up mighty heaps of earth to get ore, of gold, and of silver, and of iron, and of copper. [c]1626913104[/c] And they did work all manner of fine work. [c]1626811101[/c] [c]1626903101[/c]

places.name: Great Jaredite City
places.info: Jaredite population hub near the narrow neck of land

places.name: Narrow Neck of Land

The industriousness of the people is underscored by seven repetitions of they did work/make all manner of in just five verses.

[c]1636416602[/c] [i]3508[/i] [c]1636404101[/c] [c]1636513102[/c] And he should only live to see the fulfilling of the prophecies which had been spoken concerning another people receiving the land for their inheritance; [c]1636204801[/c] [c]1636517101[/c] [c]1636516601[/c] [c]1636512101[/c] and Coriantumr should receive a burial by them; [c]1636512102[/c] and every soul should be destroyed save it were Coriantumr. [c]1636411101[/c] [c]1636405401[/c] [c]1636413101[/c]

notes.text: This prophecy is fulfilled at Omni 1.20–22; cf. Ether 15.29–30 for Coriantumr being the last of the Jaredites.

narration.description: {Coriantumr|coriantumr2} ignores {Ether|ether}’s prophecies, and continues to wage war with his opponents; attempts on {Ether|ether}’s life are made, and his goes back to his cave to hide.

text.heading: Ether 13:22
text.content: And it came to pass that Coriantumr repented not, neither his household, neither the people; and the wars [c]1636616601[/c] ceased not; [i]2613[/i] [c]1636604101[/c] and they sought to kill Ether, [c]1636517101[/c] [c]1636604701[/c] but he fled from before them and hid again in the cavity of the rock. narration.description: A warrior name {Shared|shared} comes against {Coriantumr|coriantumr2}, and beats him, but {Coriantumr|coriantumr2}’s sons retaliate, and regain the kingdom.

text.heading: Ether 13:23–24
text.content: And it came to pass that there arose up Shared, and he also gave battle unto Coriantumr; [i]3510[/i] and he did beat him, [c]1636704701[/c] insomuch that in the third year he did bring him [c]1636716601[/c] into captivity. [c]1636704801[/c] [c]1636713101[/c] And the sons of Coriantumr, in the fourth year, [c]1636806601[/c] did beat Shared, and did obtain the kingdom again unto their father. [c]1636704101[/c]

notes.text: Nothing is known of Shared’s origins.

narration.description: War and wickedness ravage the land.

text.heading: Ether 13:25–26
text.content: Now there began to be a war upon all the face of the land, [c]1636917102[/c] [c]1636913101[/c] every man with his band fighting for that which he desired. [c]1636918101[/c] [c]1636904801[/c] [c]1636904101[/c] [c]1636904701[/c] [c]1636912101[/c] And there were robbers, [c]1637004101[/c] and in fine, all manner of wickedness upon all the face of the land. [c]1636711101[/c]

narration.description: {Coriantumr|coriantumr2} gathers his powers and attacks {Shared|shared} in the [valley of Gilgal|valley-of-gilgal]; he peruses {Shared|shared} to the [plains of Heshlon|plains-of-heshlon], and beats him after a three day battle.

text.heading: Ether 13:27–28
text.content: And it came to pass that Coriantumr was exceedingly angry with Shared, [c]1637016601[/c] and he went against him with his armies to battle; and they did meet in great anger, and they did meet in the valley of Gilgal; [c]1637116602[/c] [c]1637116601[/c] and the battle became exceedingly sore. [c]1637104701[/c] And it came to pass that Shared fought against him for the space of three days. And it came to pass that Coriantumr beat him, and did pursue him until he came to the plains of Heshlon. [c]1637216601[/c]

narration.description: {Shared|shared} fights back, and drives {Coriantumr|coriantumr2} back to the [valley of Gilgal|valley-of-gilgal]; {Coriantumr|coriantumr2} is wounded in his thigh, but still defends himself and kills {Shared|shared}.

text.heading: Ether 13:29–31
text.content: And it came to pass that Shared gave him battle again upon the plains; and behold, he did beat Coriantumr, and drove him back again to the valley of Gilgal. [c]1637111101[/c] And Coriantumr gave Shared battle again in the valley of Gilgal, [c]1637416601[/c] in which he beat Shared and slew him. and Shared wounded Coriantumr in [c]1637516601[/c] his thigh, that he did not go to battle again for the space of two years, [c]1637504701[/c] in which time all the people upon [c]1637516602[/c] the face of the land were shedding blood, [c]1637504101[/c] and there was none to [c]1637516603[/c] restrain them. [c]1637518101[/c] [c]1637411101[/c] [c]1637104101[/c]

text.heading: Ether 14:1–2
text.content: And now there began to be a great curse upon [c]1637616601[/c] all the land because of the iniquity of the people, [c]1637605401[/c] [c]1637612101[/c] [c]1637602601[/c] in which, if a man should lay his tool or his sword upon his shelf, or upon the place [c]1637616603[/c] whither he would keep it, [c]1637616602[/c] behold, upon the morrow, he could not find it, [c]1637604101[/c] so great was the curse upon the land. [c]1637604801[/c] [c]1637617102[/c] [c]1637616604[/c] Wherefore every man did cleave unto that which was his own, [i]3511[/i] with his hands, and would not borrow neither would he lend; and every man kept the hilt of his sword [c]1637716601[/c] in his right hand, [i]2037[/i] [c]1637703101[/c] in the defence of his property and his own life and [c]1637716602[/c] of his wives and children. [c]1637713101[/c] [c]1637604701[/c] [c]1637611101[/c] [c]1637712101[/c] [c]1637606601[/c]

narration.description: {Shared|shared}’s brother {Gilead|gilead} comes to {Coriantumr|coriantumr2} to avenge {Shared|shared}—they fight, and {Coriantumr|coriantumr2} drives {Shared|shared}’s brother to the wilderness of [Akish|wilderness-of-akish].

text.heading: Ether 14:3,8
text.content:
And now, after the space of two years, and after the death of Shared, behold, there arose the brother of Shared and he gave battle unto Coriantumr, [c]1637805401[/c] [c]1637804701[/c] in which Coriantumr did beat him and did pursue him to the wilderness of Akish. [c]1637813101[/c]

Now the brother of Shared, whose name was Gilead, [c]1638302601[/c] …

notes.text: The brother of Shared is identified as Gilead in Ether 14:8.

notes.text: Presumably named after the founder of secret combinations in chs. 8–9.

narration.description: The two forces fight in the wilderness of [Akish|wilderness-of-akish], where thousands die.

text.heading: Ether 14:4
text.content: And it came to pass that the brother of Shared did give battle unto him in the wilderness of Akish; [c]1637916601[/c] [c]1637804101[/c] and the battle became exceedingly sore, [c]1637818101[/c] [c]1637913101[/c] and many thousands fell by the sword.

narration.description: Some of {Coriantumr|coriantumr2}’s men get drunk and are killed by {Gilead|gilead} brother’s men, who march out of the wilderness.

text.heading: Ether 14:5
text.content: And it came to pass that Coriantumr did lay siege to the wilderness; [c]1638016601[/c] and the brother of Shared did march forth out of the wilderness by night, and slew a part of the army of Coriantumr, as they were drunken. [c]1637804801[/c]

notes.title: “Lay siege to the wilderness”
notes.text: Probably referring to a place of retreat in a wilderness region.

narration.description: {Gilead|gilead} marches to the [land of Moron|moron], and assumes {Coriantumr|coriantumr2}’s throne.

text.heading: Ether 14:6
text.content: And he came forth to the land of Moron, and placed himself upon the throne of Coriantumr. [c]1638113101[/c]

places.name: Land of Moron
places.info: North of the great land of Desolation

notes.text: The land of Moron was identified as a royal territory at Ether 7.5–6.

narration.description: {Coriantumr|coriantumr2} stays in the wilderness for two years, where he powers up his army.

text.heading: Ether 14:7
text.content: And it came to pass that Coriantumr dwelt with his army in the wilderness for the space of two years, in which he did receive great strength to his army. [c]1638204101[/c] [c]1637811101[/c]

narration.description: {Gilead|gilead} also gains power, but a secret organization plots against him, and he is killed on this throne.

text.heading: Ether 14:8–9
text.content: Now the brother of Shared, whose name was Gilead, also received great strength to his army, because of secret combinations. [c]1638204701[/c] And it came to pass that his high priest murdered him as he sat upon his throne. [c]1638418101[/c] [c]1638204801[/c] [c]1638404101[/c] [c]1638412101[/c]

narration.description: The instigator of the murder is {Gilead|gilead}’s successor, {Lib|lib2}, who is a very large man.

text.heading: Ether 14:10
text.content: And it came to pass that one of the secret combinations murdered him in a secret pass, and obtained unto himself the kingdom; and his name was Lib; and Lib was a man of great stature, more than any other man among all the people. [c]1638311101[/c] [c]1638404701[/c]

notes.title: “And it came to pass that one of the secret combinations murdered him”
notes.text: That is, the murderous high priest

notes.title: “Murdered him in a secret pass”
notes.text: That is, the high priest assassin.

narration.description: {Coriantumr|coriantumr2} comes back from out of the wilderness, and attacks {Lib|lib2}.

text.heading: Ether 14:11
text.content: And it came to pass that in the first year of Lib, Coriantumr came up unto the land of Moron, and gave battle unto Lib. [c]1638613101[/c]

places.name: Land of Moron
places.info: North of the great land of Desolation

narration.description: {Lib|lib2} injures {Coriantumr|coriantumr2}, but ultimately {Coriantumr|coriantumr2} drives {Lib|lib2} out of the kingdom and chases him to the coast.

text.heading: Ether 14:12
text.content: And it came to pass that he fought with Lib, in which Lib did smite upon his arm that he was wounded; [c]1638604101[/c] nevertheless, the army of Coriantumr did press forward upon Lib, that he fled to the borders upon the seashore. [c]1638716601[/c] [c]1638604701[/c]

notes.title: “that he fled to the borders upon”

This is Coriantumr’s second major wound; see Ether 13.31.

narration.description: The two armies fight on the seashore.

text.heading: Ether 14:13
text.content: And it came to pass that Coriantumr pursued him; and Lib gave battle unto him upon the seashore. [c]1638813101[/c]

narration.description: {Lib|lib2} gains the advantage over {Coriantumr|coriantumr2}, who escapes to the [wilderness of Akish|wilderness-of-akish].

text.heading: Ether 14:14
text.content: And it came to pass that Lib did smite the army of Coriantumr, that they fled again to the wilderness of Akish.

narration.description: {Lib|lib2} continues the pursuit, and drives {Coriantumr|coriantumr2} to the plains of [Agosh|plains-of-agosh].

text.heading: Ether 14:15
text.content: And it came to pass that Lib did pursue him until he came to the plains of Agosh. And Coriantumr had taken all the people with him as he [c]1639016601[/c] fled before Lib in that quarter of the land whither he fled. [c]1639004701[/c] [c]1639004101[/c] [c]1638611101[/c]

narration.description: {Coriantumr|coriantumr2} and {Lib|lib2} fight in the plain of [Agosh|plains-of-agosh]—{Lib|lib2} is killed, {Coriantumr|coriantumr2} retreats, and {Lib|lib2}’s brother {Shiz|shiz} takes his place.

text.heading: Ether 14:16–17
text.content: And when he had come to the plains of Agosh he gave battle unto Lib, and he smote upon him until he died; [i]3512[/i] nevertheless, the brother of Lib did come against Coriantumr in the stead thereof, [c]1638604801[/c] [c]1639216603[/c] [c]1639102601[/c] and the battle became exceedingly sore, [i]3513[/i] in the which Coriantumr fled again before the army of the brother of Lib. text.heading: Ether 14:17
text.content: And it came to pass that Shiz pursued after Coriantumr, and he did overthrow many cities, [c]1639213101[/c] and he did slay both women and [c]1639216602[/c] children, [c]1639104101[/c] and he did burn the cities. [c]1639218101[/c] [c]1639213102[/c]

narration.description: People become increasing fearful of {Shiz|shiz}.

text.heading: Ether 14:18
text.content:
And there went a fear of Shiz throughout all the land; yea, a cry went forth throughout the land—

“Who can stand before the army of Shiz?
_behold, [c]1639204801[/c] he sweepeth the earth before him!”

notes.title: “Sweepeth the earth”
notes.text: A similar metaphor appears at Isa 14.23 (2 Ne 24.23).

narration.description: People all over gather their people together to form armies.

text.heading: Ether 14:19
text.content: And it came to pass that the people began to flock together in armies, throughout all the face of the land. [c]1639404701[/c]

narration.description: Some people ally themselves with {Shiz|shiz}’s army, others with {Coriantumr|coriantumr2}’s.

text.heading: Ether 14:20
text.content: And they were divided; [c]1639404101[/c] [c]1639512101[/c] and a part of them fled to the army of Shiz, and a part of them fled to the army of Coriantumr. [c]1639518101[/c]

narration.description: The horrific destruction leaves the land is littered with dead bodies.

text.heading: Ether 14:21
text.content: And so great and lasting had been the war, and so long had been the scene of bloodshed and carnage, that the whole face of the land was covered with the bodies of the dead. [i]3514[/i] [c]1639111101[/c] [c]1639604101[/c]

notes.text: In fulfillment of Ether 11.6

notes.title: “Covered with the bodies of the dead”
notes.text: In fulfillment of Ether 11.6, and as reported at Mos 8.8; 21.26.

narration.description: The fast pace of the war leaves people unable to bury their dead.

text.heading: Ether 14:22
text.content: And so swift and speedy was the war that there was none left to bury the dead, [c]1639604801[/c] [c]1639604701[/c] but they did march forth from the shedding of blood to the shedding of blood, leaving the bodies of both men, women, and children strewed upon the face of the land, [c]1639716601[/c] to become a prey to the worms of the flesh.

narration.description: The piles of dead bodies produce an horrendous stench.

text.heading: Ether 14:23
text.content: And the scent thereof went forth upon the face of the land, [c]1639812101[/c] even upon all the face of the land; wherefore the people became troubled by day and by night, because of the scent thereof. [c]1639609101[/c]

notes.text: A similar phenomenon was reported at Alma 16.11.

narration.description: {Shiz|shiz}, determined to avenge his brother {Lib|lib2}, continues to peruse {Coriantumr|coriantumr2}.

text.heading: Ether 14:24
text.content: Nevertheless, Shiz did not cease to pursue Coriantumr; [c]1639904701[/c] [c]1639912101[/c] [c]1639913101[/c] [c]1638606601[/c] for he had sworn to avenge himself upon Coriantumr of the blood of his brother, [c]1639918101[/c] [c]1639904101[/c] who had been slain…

notes.title: “Word of the Lord…Coriantumr should not fall”
notes.text: Apparently Shiz had heard of Ether’s prophecy at Ether 13.20–21 and wanted to disprove it.

narration.description: The {Lord|god} reveals to {Ether|ether} that {Coriantumr|coriantumr2} will survive the war.

text.heading: Ether 14:24–25
text.content: …and the word of the Lord which came to Ether that Coriantumr should not fall by the sword. [c]1639916601[/c] [c]1639711101[/c] [c]1640004101[/c] And thus we see that the Lord did visit them in the fulness of his wrath, [c]1640018101[/c] [c]1640018102[/c] [c]1640005401[/c] [c]1640012101[/c] and their wickedness and abominations had prepared a way for their everlasting destruction. [c]1640009101[/c]

people.name: God
people.title: A reference to diety, be it Yahweh (יהוה); Jesus, or God the Father.

notes.title: “Thus we see…in the fulness of his wrath”
notes.text: See Ether 2.8.

narration.description: {Shiz|shiz} drives {Coriantumr|coriantumr2} to the coast, where they fight for three days.

text.heading: Ether 14:26
text.content: And it came to pass that Shiz did pursue Coriantumr eastward, even to the borders by the seashore, [c]1640116601[/c] [c]1640113101[/c] and there he gave battle unto Shiz for the space of three days.

narration.description: {Shiz|shiz}’s army is heavily hit, and retreats to the [land of Corihor|valley-of-corihor], where they kill all those who would not join them.

text.heading: Ether 14:27
text.content: And so terrible was the destruction among the armies of Shiz that the people began to be frightened, [c]1639904801[/c] [c]1640004701[/c] and began to flee before the armies of Coriantumr; and they fled to the land of Corihor, and swept off the inhabitants before them, [c]1640212101[/c] all them that would not join them. [c]1640011101[/c]

text.heading: Ether 14:28
text.content: And they pitched their tents in the valley of Corihor; [i]3515[/i] and Coriantumr pitched his tents in the valley of Shurr. Now the valley of Shurr was near the hill Comron; wherefore, Coriantumr did gather his armies together upon the hill [c]1640316601[/c] Comron, [i]3516[/i] [c]1640304101[/c] [c]1640313101[/c] and did sound a trumpet unto the armies of Shiz to invite them forth to battle. [c]1640304701[/c] [c]1640313102[/c]

narration.description: Three separate battles ensue, in which {Shiz|shiz}’s forces are severely weakened.

text.heading: Ether 14:29
text.content: And it came to pass that they came forth, but were driven again; and they came the second time, and they were driven again the second time. And it came to pass that they came again the third time, and the battle became exceedingly sore.

narration.description: {Shiz|shiz} attacks {Coriantumr|coriantumr2} personally, and inflicts many deep wounds; {Coriantumr|coriantumr2} faints, and is carried of as if dead.

text.heading: Ether 14:30
text.content: And it came to pass that Shiz smote upon Coriantumr [c]1640516601[/c] that he gave him many deep wounds; [c]1640504701[/c] [c]1640106601[/c] [c]1640504101[/c] [c]1640512101[/c] and Coriantumr, having lost his blood, fainted, and was carried away as though he were dead. [c]1640304801[/c] [i]3517[/i]

narration.description: Seeing the tremendous loss of life, {Shiz|shiz} commands his army to retreat.

text.heading: Ether 14:31
text.content: Now the loss of men, women and children on both sides was so great that Shiz commanded his people that they should not pursue the armies of Coriantumr; wherefore, they returned to their camp. [c]1640302601[/c]

narration.description: {Coriantumr|coriantumr2}, recovering from his wounds, remembers the prophesies of {Ether|ether}; seeing the millions of people dead on his account, he beings to repent.

text.heading: Ether 15:1–3
text.content: And it came to pass when Coriantumr had recovered of his wounds, he began to remember the words which Ether had spoken unto him. [c]1640717102[/c] [c]1640716601[/c] [c]1640704701[/c] [c]1640705401[/c] [c]1640702601[/c] [c]1640904101[/c] He saw that there had been slain by the sword already nearly two millions of his people, [c]1640812101[/c] [c]1640803101[/c] [c]1640813101[/c] and he began to sorrow in his heart; [c]1640816601[/c] yea, there had been slain two millions of mighty men, and also their wives and their children. [c]1640711101[/c] He began to repent of the evil which he had done; [c]1640704801[/c] [c]1640712101[/c] he began to remember the words which had been spoken by the mouth of all the prophets, and he saw them that they were fulfilled thus far, every whit; and his soul mourned and refused to be comforted. [c]1640718101[/c]

notes.text: Coriantumr’s change of heart is underscored by four repetitions of he began to in just three verses.

notes.title: “The words which Ether had spoken unto him”
notes.text: See Ether 13.20–21.

Two million deaths seems unreasonably high, particularly since there have been no conclusive traces of a large, Mesopotamian-based Jaredite civilization discovered in the New World, but see Morm 6.10–15n.
“Mourned”…“refused to be comforted”, Gen 37.34–35; Ps 77.2; Jer 31.15.

narration.description: {Coriantumr|coriantumr2} writes {Shiz|shiz} a letter asking him to surrender to prevent more lost of life—{Shiz|shiz} replies and says that if {Coriantumr|coriantumr2} offers his life up to {Shiz|shiz}, {Shiz|shiz} would spare the people.

text.heading: Ether 15:4–5
text.content: And it came to pass that he wrote an epistle unto Shiz, [c]1641004801[/c] [i]3518[/i] [c]1641013101[/c] desiring him that he would spare the people, [c]1641016601[/c] [c]1641112101[/c] and he would give up the kingdom for the sake of the lives of the people. [c]1640904701[/c] And it came to pass that when Shiz had received his epistle he wrote an epistle unto Coriantumr, that if he would give himself up, that he might slay him with his own sword, [c]1641118101[/c] [c]1641113101[/c] [c]1641104101[/c] that he would spare the lives of the people. [c]1641104701[/c] [c]1640911101[/c]

notes.text: Coriantumr had earlier rejected an offer from the Lord that would have spared his people and still left him with his kingdom (Ether 13.20); his bargaining position with Shiz is now very much reduced.
Shiz’s demand would have proven Ether’s prophecy false (see Ether 14.24n), but the counteroffer is rendered moot by the resurgence of anger in the next verse.

narration.description: Seeing this reply, {Coriantumr|coriantumr2} is furious, and begins to prepare for an attack on {Shiz|shiz}.

text.heading: Ether 15:6–7
text.content: And it came to pass that the people repented not of their iniquity; [c]1641204101[/c] and the people of Coriantumr were stirred up to anger against the people of Shiz; [c]1641216601[/c] [c]1641212101[/c] and the people of Shiz were stirred up to anger against the people of Coriantumr; wherefore, the people of Shiz did give battle unto the people of Coriantumr. [i]3519[/i] [c]1641204701[/c] And when Coriantumr saw that he was about to fall he fled again before the people of Shiz. [c]1640706601[/c]

narration.description: {Coriantumr|coriantumr2} and {Shiz|shiz} bring their armies near the [waters of Ripliancum|waters-of-ripliancum], and engage in a battle—{Coriantumr|coriantumr2} is again wounded, and faints due to blood loss.

narration.description: The two colossal armies march towards each other, initiate a battle, and fight all day long.

text.heading: Ether 15:15
text.content: And it came to pass that when they were all [c]1642116601[/c] gathered together, every one to the army which he would, with their wives and their children— [c]1642112101[/c] both men women and children being armed with weapons of war, [c]1642105401[/c] having shields, and breastplates, and head–plates, and being clothed after the manner of war—They did march forth one against another to battle; [c]1642118101[/c] [c]1642116602[/c] [i]2038[/i] [i]3524[/i] [c]1642113101[/c] and they fought all that day, and conquered not. [c]1642104701[/c] [c]1642104101[/c]

notes.text: This section recounts the last eight days of the Jaredites. The details must have been communicated to Ether, who was in hiding at the time (Ether 13.22; 15.12, 33), either by God or by Coriantumr himself. The coming of night that is mentioned eight times in Ether 15:16–25 seems both literal and metaphorical.
Some of these breastplates will be retrieved by an expedition sent out by Limhi, many centuries later; see Mos 8.10.

narration.description: At night, the fighters return to their camps and hear the sorrowed cries of their people mourning their dead.

text.heading: Ether 15:16
text.content: And it came to pass that when it was night they were weary, and retired to their camps; and after they had retired to their camps they took up a howling and a lamentation for the loss of the slain of their people; [c]1642216602[/c] [c]1642216601[/c] [i]3525[/i] [c]1641711101[/c] and so great were their cries, their howlings and lamentations, [c]1642205401[/c] that they did rend the air exceedingly.

notes.text: “A howling and a lamentation for the loss of the slain” recalls the destruction at the time of Jesus’s coming to the Nephites (3 Ne 10.2). The beginning of Jaredite civilization was marked by nighttime praises of the Lord (Ether 6.9); it ends with nocturnal howling, lamentations, and cries.

narration.description: The following day proceeds similarly, with fighting all day and mourning all night.

text.heading: Ether 15:17
text.content: And it came to pass that on the morrow they did go again to battle, [c]1642316601[/c] and great and terrible was that day; nevertheless, they conquered not, [c]1642304101[/c] [c]1642304701[/c] and when the night came again they did rend the air with their cries, [i]3526[/i] and their howlings, and their mournings, for the loss of the slain of their people.

And behold, the Spirit of the Lord had ceased striving with them, and Satan had full power over the hearts of the people; [c]1642518101[/c] [c]1642507201[/c] [c]1642505401[/c] [c]1642512101[/c] for they were given up unto the hardness of their hearts, and the blindness of their minds that they might be destroyed; [c]1642513101[/c] wherefore they went again to battle. [i]2039[/i] [c]1642411101[/c] [c]1642507202[/c]

notes.text: This is a reiteration of the offer Coriantumr made at Ether 15:4 above.

In this verse, Moroni repurposes earlier language from his account of the Jaredites to show how gross iniquity culminates in violence: “my Spirit will not always strive with man” (Ether 2.15); “Satan may have no power upon the hearts” (Ether 8.26); “hardness of heart and blindness of mind” (Ether 4.15)—though the phrases have precedents elsewhere in the BoM and the Bible.
